notes.summary: Independently checked primary inputs; analytic comparison and all-real ideal characterization on compact manifolds.
notes.detailedSummary: Identifies exact primary resolution, proper-image, divisorial subtraction, Bergman approximation, subadditivity, strong-openness, Kähler model-convergence, and local product inputs. Proves analytic ordinary comparison through global ideal resolution and proves equality of all compact divisorial Lelong numbers iff equality of every real-weight multiplier ideal. External deep theorems remain mathematical inputs, not formally certified results.
notes.text:
Verified primary inputs and analytic comparison lemmas.

Use d^c=i(barpartial-partial)/(4 pi), so dd^c=i partial barpartial/(2 pi) and dd^c log|s|^2=[s=0]. All functions mean their genuine canonical quasi-psh representatives, including values at poles.

The indispensable primary inputs were opened independently:

(i) [Bierstone–Milman, Invent. Math. 128 (1997), 207–302](https://www.mahalex.net/teaching/seminars/gabber/Bierstone-Milman%20Canonical%20desingularization%20in%20characteristic%20zero.pdf): complex-analytic category (0.1)(2), compact embedded resolution Theorem 1.6, coherent ideal principalization Theorem 1.10, and compact abstract resolution Theorem 13.2. Compactness gives finite sequences. The published full article, rather than its earlier abbreviated draft, is used.

(ii) [Grauert, Publ. Math. IHES 5 (1960)](https://www.numdam.org/item/PMIHES_1960__5__5_0.pdf), section 7, Satz 1, printed p.60: proper images of reduced complex spaces are analytic. Its primary proof identifies the image with the support of the coherent direct image of the structure sheaf.

(iii) [Siu, Invent. Math. 27 (1974)](https://people.math.harvard.edu/~siu/siu_reprints/siu_analyticity_lelong_set_invent1974.pdf): the introduction and scanned printed pp.71–75 were inspected, including Theorem 2.12(iii), Proposition 3.2 and Theorem 3.4. These give analyticity of positive Lelong level sets and divisorial subtraction: the part of a positive closed (1,1) current on a smooth prime hypersurface is its generic coefficient times that hypersurface, and subtracting it leaves a positive closed current.

(iv) [Demailly, arXiv:1401.5432v2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.5432v2), Theorems 1.2 and 1.6, Remark 1.4, Lemma 1.10, Corollary 1.12 and Theorem 4.1.5: compact Hermitian Bergman approximation, analytic local ideal types, dyadic monotonicity, and I(lambda' w_m) contained in I(lambda w) for lambda'>lambda and sufficiently large m. The construction uses exp(-2m phi); substituting phi=w/2 gives the task’s I(mw) and coefficient m^{-1}log(sum|generators|^2). Smooth corrections do not change ideals.

(v) [Demailly–Ein–Lazarsfeld](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0002035v2), analytic Theorem 2.6(ii): I(phi+psi) is contained in I(phi)I(psi). It applies locally to quasi-psh functions after bounded smooth correction and at arbitrary real weights.

(vi) [Guan–Zhou, Ann. Math. 182 (2015), 605–616](https://annals.math.princeton.edu/wp-content/uploads/annals-v182-n2-p05-p.pdf), Theorem 1.1: a germ in I(tw) belongs to I(t'w) for some t'>t on a smaller neighborhood. Its convention is exp(-w).

(vii) [Darvas–Xia, arXiv:2403.08259v2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2403.08259v2), Proposition 2.1, pp.6–7: decreasing ordinary model potentials in closed backgrounds on a compact Kähler manifold have convergent non-pluripolar masses; positive limit mass implies convergence of generic Lelong numbers on every divisor over that manifold. The statement and proof were inspected. Theorem 2.2(iv) also verifies the exact dyadic ideal coefficient. This convergence proposition is used only on P^d below.

(viii) [Bedford–Taylor, Acta Math. 149 (1982)](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~ebedford/PapersForM655/BTNewCapacity.pdf), section 2, Theorem 2.1, Corollaries 2.2 and 2.8, and Theorem 6.9: bounded local products, multilinearity, integration by parts, and zero capacity of pluripolar sets. [BEGZ](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0812.3674v2), section 1.1, formula (1.1) and Proposition 1.4: local non-pluripolar truncation and locality. The local facts are used on Hopf charts; global Kähler finiteness is not transferred to Hopf manifolds.

(ix) [Xia–Zhang, arXiv:2608.21053v1](https://arxiv.org/html/2608.21053v1), Theorem 1.1, Proposition 4.1 and its full proof: the radial family V_eta is constant at the positive end, has V_x=0 for x<=-2, has inf V_x>=-delta_eta with delta_eta tending to zero, satisfies its three positivity inequalities, and has threefold mass tending to infinity. The slope estimate follows from (4.3) and -m_eta<=g_eta'<=0 with m_eta=o(1). Their dd^c is i partial barpartial. Divide their background forms by 2 pi and KEEP the scalar potentials unchanged: omega+dd^c V=(omega_source+dd^c_source V)/(2 pi). Thus the threefold mass is divided by (2 pi)^3. No higher-dimensional assertion is imported.

Analytic comparison lemma. Let phi have a global coherent analytic singularity type on a compact manifold. If a genuine quasi-psh v satisfies nu(v composed pi,E)>=nu(phi composed pi,E) for every prime on every compact smooth modification, then v preceq phi. Resolve phi’s coherent ideal by (i). On the compact resolution, phi=L+O(1), where L is the smooth-metric logarithm of a finite effective real divisor. By (iii), subtracting its coefficients from the local positive current of v leaves a quasi-psh residual v composed pi-L with a fixed smooth lower Hessian bound. This residual is bounded above on the compact resolution. Hence v<=phi+C, including canonical pole values. Ordinary order conversely implies the Lelong inequalities.

If phi is theta-psh, P_theta[phi] is ordinarily equivalent to phi. The lower bound follows by normalizing phi. For the upper bound uniformly over competitors v<=0, use the same resolution. R_v=v composed pi-L has a common lower Hessian bound and satisfies R_v<=-L almost everywhere. Its positive part has uniformly bounded integral. Local submean estimates on finitely many charts bound sup R_v uniformly. Thus P_theta[phi]<=phi+C. The envelope has analytic singularity type and is ordinary model.

Divisorial characterization of the ideal class. For any smooth compact modification pi and prime E put A_pi(E)=1+ord_E(Jac pi). Bergman approximation gives

nu(w composed pi,E)-A_pi(E)/m <= ord_E I(mw)/m <= nu(w composed pi,E).

For the upper bound, the local extension estimate in the verified Bergman construction gives w<=w_m+O(1). For the lower bound, pull back integrability of a generator g. At generic E write g composed pi=s^r times a unit, Jac pi=s^{A-1} times a unit, and w composed pi=alpha log|s|^2+rho. The residual rho is locally bounded above after a smooth correction. The radial integral forces r-m alpha+A>0; equality already diverges. Taking the minimum generator order proves the bound. Consequently these ideal slopes converge to the generic Lelong number.

Suppose nu(v,E)>=nu(w,E) on every compact smooth modification. Resolve I(mw) globally. Since nu(w_m,E)<=nu(w,E), analytic comparison gives v preceq w_m for each m. Given a germ g in I(tv), strong openness supplies t'>t with g in I(t'v). Thus g lies in I(t'w_m), and for sufficiently large m in I(tw) by (iv). Therefore I(tv) is contained in I(tw) at every real t>0. Conversely ideal inclusions imply the divisorial inequalities through the slope bounds. Equality of all compact divisorial numbers is therefore equivalent to equality of all real-weight multiplier ideals, also on compact non-Kähler manifolds. This argument does not presume that arbitrary local modifications globalize.

These are mathematical deductions using independently checked standard primary theorems; they are not formal proofs of those external theorems. Detailed source applications are retained in source_audit.txt, retrieval responses in sources/*.json, and the full note in notes/n1.txt. Rerun public-source download attempts with python fetch_sources.py.

notes.summary: A: every scalar Hopf H_n, n>=3, fails BMP for every Hermitian form, through the verified threefold family and an all-dimensional determinant comparison.
notes.detailedSummary: Computes the full positive matrix and actual mass 2n(n-1) integral A^(n-2)Delta. The primary construction’s uniform negative-slope estimate bounds the extra angular factors below on the divergence region. Masses therefore diverge in every dimension n>=3, and scaling transfers the construction to every Hermitian background.
notes.text:
A: failure of BMP on every scalar Hopf H_n, n>=3.

Let d=n-1 and E=C/(Z+2 pi i Z). On the affine projectivization chart write z=exp(w)(1,xi), xi in C^d. Set x=log|xi|^2 and mu=exp(x)/(1+exp(x)). Let alpha=dd^c log||z||^2 and beta=d log||z||^2 wedge d^c log||z||^2. They descend because log||ez||^2 changes by 2. Alpha is normalized FS pulled back from P^d, and beta has rank one and is positive on the vertical line. Thus omega=alpha+beta is Hermitian.

Use exactly the primary radial functions V_eta verified in n1, with v_eta=V_eta. The background and dd^c operator are both the source’s ones divided by 2 pi; the scalar potential is unchanged. No new heat construction is introduced. The additional estimates give V_x=0 on x<=-2 and V_x>=-delta_eta everywhere, delta_eta tending to zero. Independence of x at the negative end and constancy in both variables at the positive end extend these functions smoothly across xi=0 and the hyperplane at infinity in every dimension.

Here is the higher-dimensional positivity calculation. Since r=w+bar w+log(1+exp x), partial r=dw+mu partial x and

alpha=(i/(2 pi))[mu partial barpartial x+mu(1-mu) partial x wedge barpartial x],

choose a radial vector in the xi-coordinate plane unit for 2 pi alpha, namely (mu(1-mu))^{-1/2} sum xi_j partial/partial xi_j, together with d-1 angular vectors unit for 2 pi alpha and annihilated by partial x, and the vertical vector partial/partial w. The radial vector is not the connection-horizontal lift. The matrix of 2 pi(omega+dd^c V_eta) has angular eigenvalue A/mu of multiplicity d-1, where A=mu+V_x, and radial/vertical block

[(mu+V_xx)/(mu(1-mu)), (mu+V_x barw)/sqrt(mu(1-mu));
 (mu+V_wx)/sqrt(mu(1-mu)), 1+V_w barw].

The source inequalities are exactly A>0, B=1+V_w barw>0, and Q=mu+V_xx-|mu+V_x barw|^2/B>0. Hence the complete matrix is positive for every d>=2. At xi=0 the additional horizontal derivatives vanish and B>0 gives positivity; where V is constant positivity is immediate.

Put Delta=(mu+V_xx)(1+V_w barw)-|mu+V_x barw|^2=BQ>0. The normalized FS radial probability density on C^d is d mu^(d-1)mu_x dx: FS^d has Lebesgue density d!/pi^d*(1+|xi|^2)^(-d-1), and spherical integration followed by |xi|^2=exp x gives the assertion. The determinant ratio to the background is (A/mu)^(d-1)Delta/mu_x. On the elliptic fiber beta has integral 2: w=s+it has periods 1 and 2 pi, and beta=ds wedge dt/pi. Angular integration is normalized to one. Thus the actual mass is

M_n(V_eta)=2 n d integral_(R x E) A^(d-1)Delta dx dA_E,

where dA_E is Haar probability measure. For V=0 this gives 2n, agreeing with integral omega^n.

For n=3,d=2, the independently verified source theorem and normalization give M_3(V_eta) tending to infinity, and integral A Delta=M_3/12. On x<=-2, all x derivatives of V vanish. Periodicity gives integral_E V_w barw=0. Therefore

integral_(-infinity,-2) integral_E A Delta dA_E dx=mu(-2)^2/2,

independently of eta. Set c0=mu(-2)/2>0. For sufficiently small eta, A>=c0 on x>=-2 by the uniform slope estimate. Hence

M_n(V_eta)>=2 n d c0^(d-2)[M_3(V_eta)/12-mu(-2)^2/2],

which tends to infinity for every n>=3. This verifies actual divergence rather than using a dimensional analogy.

For an arbitrary Hermitian h, compactness gives c>0 with h>=c omega. Then h+dd^c(c V_eta)>=c(omega+dd^c V_eta)>0, and monotonicity of smooth positive matrix determinants gives mass at least c^n M_n(V_eta). These are globally smooth real potentials. Thus v_+(h)=infinity for every h.

The source input is three-dimensional and is verified in n1; the full matrix, radial density and comparison are deductions here. verify_formulas.py checks determinants for n=3,...,8, FS densities for d=2,...,8, and normalization. These finite exact checks supplement the general proof. Evidence is in artifacts/formula_checks.json; rerun with python verify_formulas.py. Full note: notes/n2.txt.

notes.summary: B: finite compact analytic extraction for arbitrary-dimensional bases, with every ideal and quasi-psh pullback identity, including infinite residuals.
notes.detailedSummary: A finite nonnegative order of the pulled top differential decreases by (codimension-1)e whenever the smooth image center is blown up. Compact resolution and source principalization supply the required global auxiliary spaces and lifts. Termination produces a base prime F; a generic ramified normal form proves both identities for every ideal and potential with the same F and e.
notes.text:
B: finite compact analytic extraction and pullback identities.

Let f:Z->B be dominant between connected smooth compact manifolds, dim Z=m and dim B=d>=1, and let D be prime. All centers have reduced analytic structure. The proper-image theorem verified in n1 applies to the reduced compact D, so S=f(D) is compact irreducible analytic. Dominance makes the top differential nonzero.

If S=B, every nonzero coherent base ideal is a unit at generic B, so its pullback order along D is zero. The dominant restriction D->B has rank d at generic smooth D, making f a submersion there. Positive Lelong level sets of a genuine base quasi-psh function are proper analytic subsets. Dominance prevents D from lying in any of their pullbacks. Submersion preserves point Lelong numbers, so the generic pullback Lelong number along D is zero. This includes functions with poles.

Suppose S is proper. At each stage take a smooth compact base B_j and a holomorphic lift f_j from a smooth compact modification Z_j of Z that is unchanged near generic D. Write D_j for the strict prime. Define k_j as the order along D_j of the nonzero section f_j^*(dx_1 wedge ... wedge dx_d) of Omega^d_(Z_j): it is the minimum coefficient order in a smooth source frame. It is finite and nonnegative. A base coordinate change multiplies by a unit, so k_j is intrinsic near the generic image.

If S_j=f_j(D_j) has codimension one, stop. Otherwise resolve S_j inside B_j by the compact embedded theorem of n1. The resulting smooth compact B_j^r has smooth strict center S_j^r of the same codimension c>=2 and is unchanged over generic smooth S_j. Each target blowup admits a global lift after principalizing the pulled coherent center ideal on the source. The ideal is nonzero by dominance. At generic D it is already (s^e) times a unit; any source blowup affecting the whole generic divisor is a divisor blowup and hence an isomorphism. Thus the source principalization is unchanged near generic D. In target blowup charts, divide pulled generators by one of minimum order, whose quotient is a unit near generic D. This supplies the holomorphic generic lift, and the strict D dominates the strict S_j^r.

Blow up the entire smooth compact S_j^r. Let e>=1 be the order of its pulled ideal along D. With normal center coordinates x_1,...,x_c, a blowup chart has x_1=y_1, x_i=y_1 y_i for 2<=i<=c. Consequently

dx_1 wedge ... wedge dx_d=y_1^(c-1)dy_1 wedge ... wedge dy_d,

and k_new=k_old-(c-1)e. Preparation over the singular locus has zero Jacobian order at generic D; more generally every target blowup with a holomorphic generic lift only decreases k by its nonnegative Jacobian order. Each codimension-at-least-two round therefore decreases a finite nonnegative integer by at least one. There are at most k_0 rounds. If k reaches zero, another such round is impossible. For d=1 a proper image is already a divisor.

All spaces are compact because the operations are proper; their dominating smooth components are connected. Each subsequent strict-divisor image is compact analytic by proper mapping. We obtain a finite smooth compact modification sigma:B'->B and a prime F dominated by D under a holomorphic generic lift. No global algebraic function-field identification or nonproper local-image closure is used.

At generic smooth D over generic smooth F, pull back a local equation x of F. It is s^e times a unit. Dominance D->F supplies d-1 independent tangential coordinates y. Absorbing an e-th root of the unit into s and completing source coordinates gives the normal form

(s,y,z)->(s^e,y).

An ideal sigma^*b of generic order r on F factors as x^r times an ideal with a generator nonzero generically on F. Its pullback stays nonzero generically on D. Therefore ord_D(f^*b)=e ord_F(sigma^*b) for EVERY nonzero coherent b. The extracted F and e do not depend on the test ideal.

For a genuine quasi-psh w, divisorial subtraction from n1 gives, up to smooth correction,

w composed sigma=alpha log|x|^2+rho,

where alpha=nu(w composed sigma,F) and rho has generic Lelong number zero on F. The residual may be identically minus infinity on F; no restriction rho|F is taken. At very general F its point Lelong number is zero, by Siu’s analytic level sets. The normal form sends a source ball of radius r onto a set containing a base ball of radius c r^e. Thus sup_(source ball r)(rho composed f_lift)>=sup_(base ball c r^e)rho. Dividing by the negative log r^2 and using maximum-growth characterization gives nu(rho composed f_lift)<=e nu(rho,base point)=0. Nonnegativity gives zero generic residual coefficient. The logarithmic term contributes e alpha, proving

nu(w composed f,D)=e nu(w composed sigma,F).

This proves both alternatives in arbitrary base dimension, including residual potentials infinite on F. Resolution and proper-image applications are independently checked in n1; the termination invariant and identities are proved here. Full note: notes/n3.txt.

notes.summary: C: submersion multiplier ideals at every real weight and the actual restricted image-ideal identity.
notes.detailedSummary: Fubini, fiber Taylor estimates and Krull intersection in the convergent local ring prove the submersion identity without an integer-weight shortcut. Hopf projectivization then gives nu(u,Y)=0 and I(tu)O_Y=q^*(I(tU)O_B), even if U|B is identically minus infinity.
notes.text:
C: exact submersion multiplier pullback and actual image ideals.

For a holomorphic submersion f and genuine quasi-psh W on its base, product coordinates f(x,z)=x give

I(t(W composed f))=I(tW)O_source

for every real t>0. For one inclusion, express a member of the extended ideal as a finite sum of base generators times holomorphic coefficients bounded on a smaller product; Fubini proves integrability. Conversely expand an integrable holomorphic germ G(x,z) in fiber variables. Cauchy/submean estimates bound the square of each Taylor coefficient by a constant times the fiber integral of |G|^2. Since the weight depends only on x, Fubini puts every coefficient in I(tW). For each N, the finite Taylor polynomial belongs to the extended ideal and the remainder to (z)^N. Krull intersection in the Noetherian convergent local ring, applied to the quotient by the extended ideal, gives intersection_N(I(tW)O+(z)^N)=I(tW)O. Thus G belongs to the actual extended ideal, not merely its completion. Bounded smooth corrections do not affect this proof.

Projectivization p:H_(n+1)->P^n and q:H_n->B=P^(n-1) are holomorphic submersions with connected elliptic fibers, and Y=p^{-1}(B). Product-ball comparison preserves point Lelong numbers under a submersion. Taking generic points over B gives nu(p^*U,Y)=nu(U,B)=0. This uses ambient Lelong numbers and does not require U|B to exist as a genuine quasi-psh function.

Put b_t=I(tU)O_B, the image under the quotient to O_B. Apply the submersion identity to p and then take the quotient defining Y. Local generators g_i pull back as g_i(x), and their images on Y are exactly q^*(g_i|B). Hence

I(t p^*U)O_Y=q^*b_t

for every real t>0, as actual coherent image ideals. Their nonzero property under nu(U,B)=0 is part of the task’s conventions. The expression is not substituted by I(t(U|B)); it remains meaningful when U|B is identically minus infinity.

This proves C directly. Full note: notes/n4.txt.

notes.summary: D base step: full projective trace envelope, simultaneous divisorial exactness, and positive mass with explicit curvature room.
notes.detailedSummary: Restricted dyadic analytic ideals give decreasing ordinary model envelopes in a fixed a FS background. Analytic comparison identifies their limit with the full profile envelope. Resolving analytic types proves masses at least (a-K)^d; the verified Kähler model-convergence theorem then gives every divisorial equality. For a>=2K the base mass lies between (a/2)^d and a^d.
notes.text:
D, base step: full projective envelope and simultaneous exactness.

Let B=P^d with normalized kappa and let U on P^(d+1) satisfy nu(U,B)=0. Write b_t=I(tU)O_B. Choose c with dd^c U>=-c FS. The verified dyadic Bergman approximation in n1 supplies analytic U_k whose local type is 2^{-k}log(sum|generators of I(2^k U)|^2), with uniform lower curvature bounds. Discard finitely many terms and choose K>0 such that dd^c U_k>=-K FS. Restrict the analytic potentials: phi_k=U_k|B is genuine because b_(2^k) is nonzero, satisfies dd^c phi_k>=-K kappa, and has exactly the b_(2^k) type with coefficient 2^{-k}. U itself is not restricted.

For m=2^k, subadditivity followed by the actual quotient gives b_(2m) contained in b_m^2. Generator logarithms imply phi_(k+1) preceq phi_k.

Fix a>K and put W_k=P_(a kappa)[phi_k]. By n1, W_k is ordinarily equivalent to phi_k and is ordinary model. Thus W_(k+1)<=W_k. Each has supremum zero: a negative supremum would allow a positive constant to be added while preserving admissibility. The compact nonempty sets {W_k=0} are nested, so their intersection is nonempty. The decreasing limit W is therefore not identically minus infinity. It is genuine a kappa-psh and W_k->W in L1.

For any compact smooth modification sigma and prime F,

nu(W_k composed sigma,F)=ord_F(sigma^*b_(2^k))/2^k=:tau_k(F).

Subadditivity makes these numbers increasing, and the task’s intrinsic slope limit gives tau_k(F)->tau_(B,U)(F). On the fixed modification the genuine pullbacks decrease to W composed sigma, which is nontrivial by dominance, and converge in L1 with a common smooth lower Hessian bound. Lelong upper semicontinuity gives nu(W composed sigma,F)>=tau(F).

If v<=0 is any a kappa-psh competitor satisfying ALL intrinsic inequalities, then its numbers dominate those of phi_k on every compact modification. Analytic comparison in n1 yields v preceq phi_k, hence v<=W_k for every k and v<=W. Conversely W satisfies every constraint. Thus W is the FULL base envelope T_(a kappa)(U;B), before exactness is established.

The positive-mass hypothesis is verified next. An analytic potential and its ordinary envelope have the same mass in this closed background. Resolve the coherent ideal globally. Write the pullback as L+R, where L is a smooth-metric divisor logarithm and R is bounded. Removing the divisor current leaves gamma+dd^c R for fixed smooth closed gamma. The envelope has another bounded residual in the same gamma. Bounded Bedford–Taylor products give no mass to the divisor, and compact integration by parts makes either total mass integral gamma^d. The resolution can be chosen by blowups of the projective base and is Kähler; local addition and algebraic cancellation of a positive smooth form handles gamma if needed.

Outside the analytic polar set, a kappa+dd^c phi_k>=(a-K)kappa. Consequently

integral_B MA_(a kappa)(W_k)=integral_B MA_(a kappa)(phi_k)>=(a-K)^d.

Every a kappa-psh potential has mass at most a^d: bounded truncations max(w,-j) have total mass a^d by Stokes, and their non-pluripolar restrictions have at most this mass.

Apply the independently verified Darvas–Xia Proposition 2.1 from n1 ONLY on the compact Kähler B, with theta=a kappa, zero background errors, and decreasing ordinary models W_k. Its mass conclusion gives integral MA(W)>=(a-K)^d>0. Its positive-mass conclusion now applies and gives, for EVERY prime F over B,

nu(W composed sigma,F)=lim_k nu(W_k composed sigma,F)=tau_(B,U)(F).

Thus equality does not follow merely from upper semicontinuity. For a>=a0=2K,

(a/2)^d<=integral_B MA_(a kappa)(W)<=a^d.

The room K depends on the ambient curvature bound and the analytic approximation. No mass theorem is applied on a Hopf manifold or an arbitrary non-Kähler modification. Full argument: notes/n5.txt; exact primary applications: source_audit.txt.

notes.summary: D: full Hopf-envelope pullback and exactness on every modification and larger Hermitian background; targets are non-Kähler and fail BMP.
notes.detailedSummary: General extraction checks every target prime, and smooth compact fiber products check every base prime. Elliptic fiber maxima handle all competitors and prove the normalized full envelope equals the pulled projective envelope. Exactness extends to every Hermitian background dominating a sufficiently large invariant one. The theorem remains scoped to scalar Hopf geometry and the basic data in C.
notes.text:
D: full invariant envelope and every modified divisor.

Use C with n>=3,d=n-1. On Y=H_n let r=log||z||^2 modulo 2. Its differentials dr,d^c r are global. Set alpha=q^*kappa and beta=dr wedge d^c r. Their kernels are complementary, so Omega_(a,b)=a alpha+b beta is Hermitian for a,b>0. The compact connected elliptic group G=C^*/<e> acts by scalar multiplication, preserves these forms, and is transitive on each fiber. Invariant genuine potentials are precisely q^*psi.

For genuine base psi,

Omega_(a,b)+dd^c q^*psi=q^*(a kappa+dd^c psi)+b beta,

and positivity is equivalent to a kappa+dd^c psi>=0. To prove the reverse implication for currents, use a local trivialization r=w+bar w+f(x) and test on smooth horizontal vector fields (xi,-partial f(xi)). These annihilate partial r and project arbitrarily to the base. Integrating against a nonnegative vertical test measure proves positivity of the base current.

Fix ANY smooth compact target modification pi:Z->Y and prime D. Apply n3 to f=q composed pi. By n4, pulled target image ideals are f^*b_t. Horizontal primes have all orders and basic Lelong numbers zero. Otherwise n3 supplies a compact smooth base modification sigma, prime F and integer e>=1, independent of t and psi, with

tau_(Y,u)(D)=e tau_(B,U)(F),
nu(q^*psi composed pi,D)=e nu(psi composed sigma,F).

The first follows by dividing the identity for every b_t by t; the second includes residuals infinite on F. Every base competitor therefore pulls back to a target competitor with EVERY target divisor checked.

Conversely, for any compact smooth sigma:B'->B form Y'=Y x_B B'. It is smooth because q is a submersion, compact, and connected because its base and elliptic fibers are connected. Its proper map to Y is a modification, being an isomorphism over the dense open locus of sigma. The inverse image of a prime F has a unique prime dominating F: over smooth F it is a locally trivial connected elliptic bundle, whose closure is irreducible. That prime has e=1 and detects precisely the base orders and Lelong numbers. Thus every basic target competitor gives a base competitor on every base modification.

Now handle ALL target competitors. For normalized v define vhat(x)=max_(g in G)v(gx). Compactness makes it upper semicontinuous; the locally bounded-above supremum theorem makes it Omega_(a,b)-psh. It is basic and dominates v. Every translate preserves the constraints: g composed pi is another permitted modification and q composed g=q leaves every pulled b_t unchanged. Finite maxima preserve the lower divisor coefficients, and so does their increasing canonical limit. On each fixed modification, an increasing Choquet sequence of finite maxima has a common genuine lower bound and smooth lower Hessian bound. Its L1 limit agrees with the canonical pullback off the exceptional set and hence everywhere. Subtracting each prescribed coefficient leaves a positive local current in the limit. This verifies every constraint without a finite-family shortcut or BMP.

Write vhat=q^*psi. Positivity and the fiber-product argument make psi a full base competitor. Hence every v is bounded above by q^*T_(a kappa)(U;B). Conversely that pullback is a target competitor. For all a>=a0 from n5 and b>0,

T_(Omega_(a,b))(u;Y)=q^*T_(a kappa)(U;B)

as FULL normalized envelopes. Combining n3 and exactness in n5 gives every intrinsic target number on every target modification, including every exceptional prime.

For any Hermitian Omega>=Omega_(a,b), the exact pullback is an Omega-psh competitor. Thus T_Omega dominates it, giving nu(T_Omega composed pi,D)<=tau(D). The increasing-maxima argument retains all lower constraints for T_Omega, using this common genuine competitor. Equality follows simultaneously for all pi,D.

Finally H_n is diffeomorphic to S^(2n-1) x S^1, so H^2(H_n,R)=0 for n>=2. A Kähler form would be exact and have zero top integral by Stokes, contradicting positivity. The targets are therefore genuinely non-Kähler; n2 proves failure of BMP for every Hermitian form when n>=3. This supplies a sufficient condition with projective base dimension d>=2, beyond curve and curve-fibration cases. Its scope remains the basic data and scalar Hopf geometry in C.

notes.detailedSummary: Direct bounded truncation gives mass 2nb times the base mass. Exact divisorial data imply all-real ideal-class independence and model fixedness. notes.text:
E: individual mass, compatible type, addition, pullback and approximation.

Let W=T_(a kappa)(U;B) and T=q^*W, with a>=2K,b>0. For ANY genuine a kappa-psh psi, put psi_j=max(psi,-j). Bounded local multilinearity, beta^2=0 and d=n-1 give

(Omega_(a,b)+dd^c q^*psi_j)^n=nb beta wedge q^*((a kappa+dd^c psi_j)^d).

This also holds for extended products with smooth-background corrections: locally add a smooth closed positive form, apply bounded multilinearity, then cancel it algebraically. Omega need not be closed. Restrict to {q^*psi>-j} and pass to the local non-pluripolar limit. Thus

MA_(Omega_(a,b))(q^*psi)=nb beta wedge q^*MA_(a kappa)(psi).

On E, w=s+it has periods 1 and 2 pi; r=2s+constant and d^c r=dt/(2 pi). Therefore beta=ds wedge dt/pi and q_*beta=2. Consequently

integral_Y MA_(Omega_(a,b))(T)=2nb integral_B MA_(a kappa)(W),

and n5 gives

2nb(a/2)^d<=integral_Y MA_(Omega_(a,b))(T)<=2nb a^d.

These are positive finite INDIVIDUAL masses. No BMP-dependent unbounded product theorem is applied on Y.

Compatible type. Every envelope in the invariant backgrounds and larger backgrounds of n6 has the same intrinsic divisorial profile. By n1 their multiplier ideals agree at EVERY real weight. The resulting ideal class depends only on the ambient ideal class, since that class fixes every image ideal b_t. This proves ideal-class independence within the stated large backgrounds.

In each fixed background the envelope is both ordinary model and ideal model. Any ordinary competitor for P_Omega[T] has divisorial numbers at least those of T and hence belongs to the full profile family, so is <=T. T itself is a competitor. Any ideal-equivalent competitor for P_Omega[T]_I has exactly the same numbers by n1, giving the same conclusion. Thus P_Omega[T]=P_Omega[T]_I=T. Ordinary equivalence between different backgrounds is not established.

Addition. Let U_1,U_2 have zero generic Lelong number on B. Choose sufficient room for each and their sum, with Omega_i=a_i alpha+b_i beta admissible as in n6. Then T_1+T_2 is (Omega_1+Omega_2)-psh, normalized <=0, and has exact profile tau_1+tau_2=tau_(Y,u_1+u_2), by generic Lelong additivity and the task’s intrinsic additivity. In any sufficiently large admissible Omega dominating Omega_1+Omega_2, the full sum envelope dominates T_1+T_2 and has the same exact profile. By n1 it is ideal-equivalent to T_1+T_2 at every real weight. This states addition with the necessary curvature room.

For lambda>0, the bijection v->lambda v between normalized competitors, together with background and profile scaling, gives the actual equality

T_(lambda Omega)(lambda u;Y)=lambda T_Omega(u;Y).

In other permitted large backgrounds this gives equality of ideal classes.

Full ordinary pullback. For any genuine a kappa-psh phi, a competitor v<=0 with v preceq q^*phi can be replaced by its fiber maximum. The same ordinary comparison constant works for every translate because q^*phi is invariant, including at common poles. The resulting vhat=q^*psi has psi<=0, a kappa-psh and psi preceq phi. Every base competitor conversely pulls back. Therefore

P_(Omega_(a,b))[q^*phi]=q^*P_(a kappa)[phi].

With pointwise comparison against a basic obstacle f, the same proof gives P_(Omega_(a,b))(q^*f)=q^*P_(a kappa)(f) whenever a genuine competitor exists. Both statements concern all competitors.

Full dyadic approximation. Use U_k and phi_k from n5. By n4, p^*U_k has analytic type governed by I(2^k u), and its restriction is q^*phi_k. Define

Psi_k=P_(Omega_(a,b))[q^*phi_k]=q^*W_k.

The equality follows from full ordinary pullback. Each Psi_k is an ordinary model of analytic singularity type. The entire dyadic tail decreases to T and converges in L1 on Y.

On ANY compact smooth modification pi:Z->Y, the genuine pullbacks decrease to T composed pi. The limit is nontrivial because q composed pi is dominant. Quasi-psh integrability and domination of the differences by Psi_(k0) composed pi-T composed pi give L1 convergence against any smooth volume on Z. For ANY prime D, use the extraction of n3 for q composed pi, independent of k. Horizontal numbers vanish; otherwise

nu(Psi_k composed pi,D)=e ord_F(sigma^*b_(2^k))/2^k
=ord_D(pi^*(I(2^k u)O_Y))/2^k -> tau_(Y,u)(D).

Thus every modified generic number converges, as well as the full potentials in L1. This uses actual image ideals and base model convergence, not individual target mass as a substitute for exactness.

notes.summary: F: exact all-real point image ideals and all-divisor profile; the genuine basic potential has actual mass 2nb(a^d-1).
notes.detailedSummary: Radial integrability gives b_t=m_P^max(floor(t-d+1),0), including boundary weights. Every modified prime has profile ord_D(q^*m_P), realized by q^*(U|B). Resolving the point ideal and computing exceptional intersections gives base mass a^d-1, hence target mass 2nb(a^d-1) for a>1. Equality with the normalized envelope is not asserted.
notes.text:
F: point image ideals, every modified order and actual mass.

Let n>=3,d=n-1 and U=log[(sum_(i=0)^(n-2)|z_i|^2)/(sum_(i=0)^n|z_i|^2)]. This is genuine FS-psh with analytic singularities on the line where z_0,...,z_(n-2) vanish. B={z_n=0} is not contained in that line, so nu(U,B)=0. Its intersection with B is P=[0:...:0:1] in B’s coordinates.

Near P use z_(n-1)=1, x=(z_0,...,z_(n-2)) in C^d and y=z_n. Then U=log|x|^2-log(1+|x|^2+|y|^2). The second term is smooth and bounded. A holomorphic germ with first nonzero homogeneous x-degree k is integrable against exp(-tU) precisely when integral_0^epsilon rho^(2k-2t+2d-1)d rho is finite, equivalently k>t-d. Sufficiency follows from a bound C|x|^k. Necessity follows from spherical orthogonality and the positive square integral of the first nonzero homogeneous term. A coefficient that vanishes at y=0 but is nonzero as a y-germ still has positive square integral on a smaller y-ball and gives the same divergence.

Thus the ambient ideal is (x)^k(t), where k(t)=max(floor(t-d+1),0). The strict inequality includes the logarithmically divergent boundary t=k+d. Taking the actual quotient y=0 gives globally on B

b_t=I(tU)O_B=m_P^max(floor(t-d+1),0)

for EVERY real t>0.

By n4, a_t=q^*m_P^k(t). For every smooth compact target modification pi and prime D its order is k(t)ord_D(pi^*q^*m_P). Since k(t)/t tends to 1,

tau_(Y,u)(D)=ord_D(pi^*q^*m_P).

This includes every exceptional prime. Here W=U|B is genuine, kappa-psh and logarithmic of m_P. Thus q^*W is Omega_(a,b)-psh for a>=1,b>0. At generic D its pulled ideal is s^r times a tuple with a nonzero component, so q^*W composed pi=r log|s|^2+bounded. Its generic Lelong number is r, giving an exact realizer on every modification.

For its actual mass let mu:Bl_P B->B have exceptional E, and let rho:Bl_P B->P^(d-1) extend projection from P. Put H=mu^*kappa and gamma=rho^*FS. Factoring x by the exceptional coordinate in blowup charts gives

dd^c(W composed mu)=[E]+gamma-H.

The numerator contributes the exceptional logarithm and the FS potential of the x-directions; the denominator contributes -H. Off E the pulled a kappa-current is the smooth form (a-1)H+gamma, positive for a>1, with no bounded-product mass on E. The non-pluripolar total mass is therefore

integral_B MA_(a kappa)(W)=integral_(Bl_P B)((a-1)H+gamma)^d=(aH-E)^d.

H^d integrates to 1 because mu has degree one. H restricts to zero on E because mu|E is constant, so mixed H^(d-k)E^k integrate to zero for 0<k<d. Blowup charts identify O(E)|E=O_(P^(d-1))(-1), giving integral E^d=(-1)^(d-1). Hence (aH-E)^d=a^d-1.

The direct local fiber formula in n7 applies to this W, yielding

integral_Y MA_(Omega_(a,b))(q^*W)=2nb(a^d-1), a>1,b>0.

Equality of this potential with the normalized full trace envelope is not claimed. Nor does this computation determine extremal masses over its ordinary class.

Scope, reproducibility and remaining gaps.

Notes n1–n8 supply scoped independent proof drafts of A–F using the identified, independently inspected primary theorems. They include the all-dimensional Hopf BMP construction, arbitrary-base-dimensional finite extraction, every-real-weight submersion identity, every modified divisorial order, full normalized envelopes, actual individual masses, compatible ideal type and algebra, full ordinary pullback and full dyadic convergence.

The exactness theorem is restricted to scalar Hopf targets and the basic ambient data in C, with projective base dimension d>=2. The targets are proved non-Kähler and fail BMP. This gives a sufficient condition beyond the listed curve and curve-fibration cases.

Unrestricted P18 remains OPEN here. These notes supply neither simultaneous realization on every compact non-Kähler target lacking a mass property nor an actual counterexample to that unrestricted statement. Ordinary-type independence between backgrounds and extremal ordinary singularity volumes are not established. The positive finite masses are individual envelope or realizer masses. Deep primary theorems remain mathematical inputs; source/application inspection and successful execution are not formal correctness certificates. These are unverified drafts.
